conditions_text: Brazilians with an ordinary passport do not need a visa for tourism or business in Thailand for up to 90 days (Brazilian foreign ministry, page updated 24 July 2026), under a bilateral agreement. Brazil is not on Thailand's general 30-day exemption list, and Thailand's tourism authority states that separate bilateral arrangements of 90, 30 or 14 days continue to apply, so the 15 September 2026 change does not cut Brazil to 30 days. The passport must have at least six months' validity. Leaving and re-entering within the 90 days requires being able to show the return is for tourism. All foreign travellers must also complete Thailand's Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online before arrival, within the 3 days (72 hours) before they arrive.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-exempt entry. The TDAC is free of charge on the official Immigration Bureau portal (tdac.immigration.go.th). Stays beyond 90 days require a visa from the Royal Thai Embassy in Brasilia.

conditions_text: India is not on Vietnam's visa-exemption lists (the Vietnamese Embassy in New Delhi's exemption page names no exemption for Indian citizens). Vietnam issues e-visas to nationals of all countries; apply online before travel (valid for a maximum of 90 days, single or multiple entry). You can enter and leave only through the approved air, land and sea border gates (13 airports, 16 land and 13 sea gates) - the e-visa works only at the entry/exit points you select. Passport needs at least 6 months' validity.
fee_notes: USD 25 for a single-entry visa and USD 50 for a multiple-entry visa valid under 90 days, per the Ministry of Finance fee schedule (Circular 28/2026/TT-BTC, in force from 1 April 2026; the e-visa portal pages do not itemise the amount, so confirm on the payment screen). Paid online through the portal's payment gateway; not refunded if the application is refused. Beware look-alike sites that add service fees.

conditions_text: UK citizens are on Vietnam's unilateral visa-exemption list (Resolution 44/NQ-CP): a temporary stay of up to 45 days from the date of entry, regardless of passport type and entry purpose, in force from 15 March 2025 to 14 March 2028, provided all Vietnamese entry conditions are met. UK FCDO advises passport validity of at least 6 months after arrival and 2 blank pages, and to check that the exit date on your entry stamp is 45 days from arrival. For stays beyond 45 days apply for an e-visa (up to 90 days).
fee_notes: Free; no visa application needed for stays up to 45 days. An e-visa (fee-based, up to 90 days) is needed for a longer stay, and Resolution 44/NQ-CP runs only to 14 March 2028.

Entry is at the discretion of Vietnam Immigration. Passport should have at least 6 months' validity; the Vietnamese embassy has also required a return or onward ticket. For stays beyond 30 days apply for an e-visa (up to 90 days).
fee_notes: Free; no visa application needed for stays up to 30 days. An e-visa (USD 25 single / USD 50 multiple under the fee schedule in force from 1 April 2026) is needed for a longer stay.

conditions_text: India is on the Egyptian e-visa portal's list of nationalities that may apply for a tourist e-visa, which is the route to rely on. The portal says to apply at least 7 days before departure, and that the passport must be valid at least 6 months from the arrival date. Some visa-on-arrival access for Indians holding a used US, UK or Schengen visa is reported by agencies, but no official Egyptian or Indian government page confirming the conditions could be read, so do not plan around it. Agencies also report that an Egyptian travel agent's Letter of Guarantee may be asked for; this is not stated on the public portal pages, so check at application.
fee_notes: The portal's FAQ page lists a single-entry tourism e-visa at $25 and multiple-entry at $60, paid by card online; press reports from April 2026 say the portal now charges $30 and $65. Confirm the price on visa2egypt.gov.eg before paying. The 30-day stay is the standard tourist visa length given by Canada's and the UK's advice; the portal pages read did not state it.

conditions_text: US citizens are on the Egyptian e-visa portal's eligible list, so a tourist e-visa can be applied for online in advance (apply at least 7 days before departure). A visa on arrival is also sold at approved airports; the UK government describes it as a 30-day, cash-only visa. Passport must be valid at least 6 months from the arrival date. The US State Department pages could not be opened (403), so US-specific advice was not read directly.
fee_notes: Portal FAQ lists single-entry e-visa at $25 and multiple-entry at $60; press reports from April 2026 say the portal now charges $30 and $65, so confirm on the portal. Visa on arrival: $30 USD cash (per FCDO). From 1 August 2026 Cairo airport also offers a card-only digital visa on arrival for $36 including a $6 service fee (per FCDO).

conditions_text: British passport holders can get a tourist e-visa in advance (valid for up to 3 months) or buy a visa on arrival from kiosks before immigration at approved airports, valid up to 30 days. Arrivals by air at Sharm El-Sheikh staying under 15 days in Sharm El-Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba get a free entry permission stamp and need no visa; travelling beyond those resorts requires a visa. Passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival and have at least one blank page.
fee_notes: Visa on arrival: $30 USD, cash only. At Cairo airport from 1 August 2026, a digital visa on arrival is available by card only for $36 including a $6 digital service fee. FCDO does not give the e-visa price; the portal's FAQ page lists $25 single entry, though press reports from April 2026 say $30.

conditions_text: Global Affairs Canada (page updated 26 May 2026) says Canadian passport holders can obtain an electronic visa prior to travel or a 30-day tourist visa on arrival in Egypt. Caveat: the nationality list on the Egyptian e-visa portal's FAQ page does not show Canada, so check eligibility on visa2egypt.gov.eg when you apply. Arrival visas must be paid in cash, US dollars only. At the Taba land border a 14-day visa-free entry stamp is available if staying within the Sinai Peninsula. Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Egypt. Overstaying the 30-day period can mean a fine on departure.
fee_notes: Canada's advice says entry may cost between $60 and $100 USD per person depending on travel plans (stated alongside the Taba crossing notes); visa on arrival is cash USD only. The e-visa fee is paid online; the portal FAQ lists $25 single entry, though press reports from April 2026 say $30.

conditions_text: Australian passport holders are on the Egyptian e-visa portal's list and can apply online in advance (at least 7 days before departure). The Egyptian Consulate General in Sydney lists applying for an e-visa or obtaining a visa on arrival as the options for Australian passport holders, and says the consulate itself is currently unable to issue visas. Passport must be valid at least 6 months from the arrival date. The Cairo digital visa-on-arrival kiosk (card payment, from 1 August 2026) is described in UK government advice for all arrivals at Cairo.
fee_notes: The consulate page gives no fees. Portal FAQ lists single-entry e-visa at $25 and multiple-entry at $60; press reports from April 2026 say $30 and $65. Visa on arrival is $30 USD cash and the Cairo digital version $36 by card (per FCDO).

conditions_text: Germany is on the Egyptian e-visa portal's list of nationalities that may apply for a tourist e-visa; apply online at least 7 days before departure. Passport must be valid at least 6 months from the arrival date. A visa on arrival at airports is generally offered to nationalities such as these, but no official page naming German passports was readable, so the e-visa is the confirmed route.

conditions_text: Indian citizens need a visa and are in Category A of Morocco's e-visa scheme, so they can apply online at acces-maroc.ma with an ordinary passport valid for at least 90 days from the date of the application; no US/UK/Schengen visa or residence permit is needed for this route (India has been eligible since 10 January 2023). The e-visa is for tourism or business, is valid for a maximum of 180 days from issue, is for a single entry and a stay of no more than 30 days, and stays from several e-visas cannot be added together. Processing is 24 hours (express) or 72 hours (standard), counted in Moroccan working days. An e-visa does not guarantee entry: at the border you may be asked for a return ticket, proof of means (an international bank card or cash equivalent to more than 70 euros per person per day) and hospital/repatriation insurance for the stay.
fee_notes: Fee is charged on the acces-maroc.ma portal at payment and is non-refundable once the application is validated and paid; the amount was not stated on any official page that could be opened, so it is not given here (secondary reports quote 770 MAD standard / 1,100 MAD express - check the portal). The Indian embassy page says the e-visa can be extended up to six months with multiple entries, but the official conditions say single entry and 30 days; do not rely on an extension.

conditions_text: Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular portal lists the United States of America among the countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa, and the Moroccan National Tourist Office states that for all nationalities the maximum duration of a tourist trip is 90 days, with an extension requestable at the nearest police station for a further 90 days. The Tourist Office says a valid passport must cover at least the duration of the stay. The US State Department page (reported elsewhere to ask for six months' validity and a blank page) could not be opened, so the six-month figure is not confirmed from an official page read for this rule; six months is the safer margin. No onward-ticket or accommodation requirement is stated on the pages read. Entry conditions can change at short notice.

British passport holders can visit Morocco without a visa for up to 90 days for tourism; to stay longer you must request an extension at a Moroccan police station, and non-tourism travel should be checked with the Moroccan Consulate General in the UK. UK FCDO says the passport must have an expiry date at least 3 months after the date of arrival (other governments, and some airlines, quote six months, so six months is the safer margin), and that entry has been denied to some travellers with damaged passports. FCDO lists no traveller or arrival form; foreign currency of 100,000 MAD or more must be declared on entry or exit. Rule read from the UK FCDO page because Moroccan government pages block automated access.

Canadian citizens do not need a tourist, business or student visa for stays of less than 90 days. Global Affairs Canada says a regular Canadian passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Morocco (airline rules may be stricter). To stay beyond 90 days you must get authorisation from the local police station's foreigners' service at least 15 days before the limit; overstaying can lead to detention and a fine. The page lists no entry or exit form. Rule read from Global Affairs Canada because Moroccan government pages block automated access.

Australian citizens are on Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa. Smartraveller says Australians generally do not need a visa to visit Morocco for less than 90 days, and the Moroccan National Tourist Office says the maximum duration of a tourist trip is 90 days for all nationalities (extension possible at a police station). Smartraveller says to contact a Moroccan embassy because entry conditions can change at short notice; its general note that many countries want 6 months' passport validity is not a Morocco-specific rule, and the Tourist Office only says the passport must cover the stay, so six months is the safer margin. Get the passport stamped on entry, as Smartraveller reports tourists having trouble leaving without one.

German citizens need no visa for tourist or business stays of up to 90 days (this is not EU freedom of movement; Morocco is outside the EU). Entry requires a passport, provisional passport or children's passport; a Personalausweis (identity card) is not accepted, and travellers refused on this basis must take the next flight back. The travel document must be valid for at least six months on arrival (Auswaertiges Amt), and entry is refused for a damaged passport or an incomplete machine-readable zone. Overstaying breaches Moroccan residence law and is prosecuted; extensions are decided by the foreigners' police and must be filed before the 90 days end. The page lists no entry form; foreign currency of 100,000 MAD equivalent or more must be declared.

Singapore MFA states Singaporeans can visit Morocco for up to 90 days without a visa, and Singapore is on Morocco's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries whose citizens are exempt from an entry visa. Singapore MFA's page was last modified 30 July 2026 and says entry requirements can change at short notice. It does not state a passport-validity or blank-page rule; the Moroccan National Tourist Office only says a valid passport must cover the duration of the stay, so six months' validity is the safer margin.

Brazilian citizens do not need a visa to enter and stay in Morocco for up to 90 days. The Brazilian Embassy in Rabat states the passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival in Morocco. The embassy also reports Brazilians travelling from Europe being stopped from boarding their return flight because of an irregular or undefined immigration status in Europe, so check your own status before travelling. Rule read from the Brazilian Embassy in Rabat page, not a Moroccan government page.

Indian passport holders are on the EU list of nationalities that need a visa to cross the Schengen external border (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806). For tourism a Schengen short-stay visa must be applied for in advance through the official France-Visas service (france-visas.gouv.fr), with an appointment and supporting documents; it allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. A France-Visas notice also says holders of a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by a Schengen state do not need a short-stay visa. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the official ETIAS website says it is not in operation).

No visa needed for short stays in France (Schengen area) of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area. The EU Entry/Exit System registers photo and fingerprints at the Schengen border; France-Diplomatie states it has been fully operational since 10 April 2026. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) states it is currently not in operation and that no applications are being collected, and that the EU will announce the start date several months before launch; France-Diplomatie (page updated April 2026) says it is expected in the last quarter of 2026. Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change.

Indian passport holders need a Schengen short-stay visa for tourism in Italy, applied for in advance through the Italian Embassy in New Delhi or the Consulates General in Mumbai, Bangalore or Kolkata according to your consular district (the Italian foreign ministry's visa questionnaire at vistoperitalia.esteri.it, nationality India, residence India, up to 90 days, tourism, lists these offices). It allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. The questionnaire's document list includes a passport valid at least three months beyond the requested visa, a return ticket or booking, proof of means of subsistence, proof of accommodation and health insurance of at least EUR 30,000 covering the whole Schengen area. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities (the official ETIAS site describes it as for visa-exempt travellers) and is not in operation today: the site states it is currently not in operation and no applications are collected (checked 17 October 2026). The EU Entry/Exit System has been operational since 12 October 2025 per the Italian visa site.
fee_notes: EUR 90 'Visto Schengen' fee listed by the Italian foreign ministry's visa site as the administrative cost of processing; except in special cases it is paid in the national currency of the country where you apply. Other service charges are not stated there.

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourism in Italy (Schengen area) for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. The Italian foreign ministry's visa questionnaire (vistoperitalia.esteri.it, tourism, up to 90 days) says you can enter with a passport valid at least three months after your intended departure from the Schengen area, and that border officers will ask for documents justifying the reason and length of your stay. The UK FCDO's Schengen guidance also requires the passport to have been issued within the previous 10 years. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) registers non-EU travellers at the Schengen external border (photo and fingerprints); the Italian foreign ministry's visa site says it has been operational since 12 October 2025 and the EU site lists Italy among the countries using it. If you arrive from another Schengen country rather than directly from outside, the Italian foreign ministry's visa site says foreign nationals must file a declaration of presence within 8 days at the Questura of the province; in a hotel, the declaration signed before the hotelier counts. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked on 17 October 2026) states it is currently not in operation and that no applications for travel authorisations are being collected, and that the EU will announce the start date several months before launch; the page no longer gives a launch quarter. When it starts the same site lists a EUR 20 fee. Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change.

The Spanish Foreign Ministry's conditions page says a valid residence permit or long-stay visa issued by a Schengen state removes the need for a short-stay visa, and that the passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid 3 months beyond departure. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the European Commission states it is not in operation).

No visa needed for short stays in Spain (Schengen area) of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. Per the Spanish Foreign Ministry's conditions-for-entry page, the passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area; border officers can also ask for proof of the purpose of the stay and sufficient funds (the page quotes 122 EUR per person per day for 2026, at least 1,099 EUR for stays of 9 days or more). The EU Entry/Exit System may register your photo and fingerprints at the border. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: the European Commission's ETIAS page states it is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point, and that the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. A Spanish Foreign Ministry consulate page still says it is expected in the last quarter of 2026, but no start date has been announced; do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change.

Indian passport holders appear on the Portuguese visa portal's 'List of nationalities who must be in possession of a visa' (page last updated 1 September 2025). For tourism a Schengen short-stay visa must be obtained in advance; the Schengen short-stay limit is 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, and the visa itself may be issued for fewer days. The same portal says holders of a valid uniform visa, long-stay national visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen member state are exempt from the airport transit visa requirement; it does not state a wider short-stay exemption, so check the portal. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (France-Diplomatie, updated 22 April 2026: not yet operational, scheduled for end of 2026).

Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (UK FCDO entry requirements for Portugal). The EU Entry/Exit System registers a photo and fingerprints at the border; the Portuguese visa portal says it has been fully in place at Portuguese air and sea border crossings since 10 April 2026. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: France-Diplomatie's official page, updated 22 April 2026, says the ETIAS system is not yet operational and is scheduled to launch at the end of 2026; the Portuguese visa portal (vistos.mne.gov.pt) lists no ETIAS requirement, and no start date was found. The official EU ETIAS site (travel-europe.europa.eu) could not be read by our fetcher, so confirm there before booking, and do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now.

No visa needed for tourism and other short-stay purposes. Two official texts apply. The Portuguese visa portal (vistos.mne.gov.pt) lists Brazil among nationalities exempt from a short-stay visa. The Brazil-Portugal bilateral visa-exemption agreement (promulgated in Brazil by Decreto 6.427/2008, cited here) exempts holders of ordinary passports for stays of up to 90 days, and Article 1(3) says the 90 days may be extended for an equal term under the law of the country of entry if entry and stay conditions still hold, with a total not above 180 days per year. So the official bilateral figure is 90 days, extendable (not automatically) to a 180-day-per-year ceiling; the Schengen 90-in-180 rule is the baseline, and an extension has to be requested from Portuguese authorities (AIMA), so confirm it with them before planning beyond 90 days. Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (UK FCDO entry requirements for Portugal). The EU Entry/Exit System registers a photo and fingerprints at the border; the Portuguese visa portal says it has been fully in place at Portuguese air and sea border crossings since 10 April 2026. Indian passport holders need a visa to visit the UK and are not on the ETA-eligible list: the GOV.UK page on who can apply for an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) lists the United States, Canada, Australia, Germany, Singapore and Brazil among others but not India, and says other nationalities cannot get an ETA and should check if they need a visa instead. The UK visa requirements list for carriers lists India among nationals who need a visa to enter or transit the UK. For tourism, apply online for a Standard Visitor visa before you travel; GOV.UK says the earliest you can apply is 3 months before travel, and that you can usually stay in the UK for up to 6 months. A Standard Visitor visa costs 135 GBP for up to 6 months. Check GOV.UK for the current application steps and processing times, which are not covered here.
fee_notes: Standard Visitor visa 135 GBP for up to 6 months (GOV.UK Standard Visitor visa page, checked 2026-10-17).

conditions_text: No visa is needed for a visit, but a USA passport holder must hold an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travelling to the UK. The ETA is in force today: the Immigration Rules ETA national list requires it for USA nationals travelling on or after 8 January 2025. GOV.UK says an ETA lets you travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months, and the Immigration Rules say it lasts two years from grant (or until the passport used in the application expires, if sooner) and allows multiple journeys, each visit capped at six months. It is tied to the passport used to apply, so a new passport needs a new ETA. Each traveller needs one, including babies and children. An ETA does not guarantee entry. Apply only through GOV.UK or the official UK ETA app; other websites charge extra.
fee_notes: ETA fee is 20 GBP per person (GOV.UK, ETA page, checked 2026-10-17); other sites may charge more.

conditions_text: IRCC lists India among the countries whose citizens need a valid visitor visa and a valid passport to visit or transit through Canada. India is not on IRCC's list of visa-required countries whose citizens may be eligible for an eTA (that list includes Brazil, Mexico, Philippines, Thailand and others), so holding a US visa does not substitute for a Canadian visitor visa for Indian passport holders. Apply for the visitor visa before travelling. (Checked on the IRCC eTA eligibility page, which lists the eligible visa-required countries and does not include India.)

IRCC: 'You don't need a visa or an eTA to travel to Canada' if you are a US national (US lawful permanent residents are also exempt). A valid US passport is recommended and is needed to fly; US citizens arriving by land or sea must carry proper identification showing citizenship. You must still meet Canada's basic entry requirements at the border. The permitted length of stay is not stated on the IRCC pages checked, so max stay is left blank.

British citizens (the UK passport categories IRCC lists, e.g. British citizen) are visa-exempt for Canada but need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) to fly to or transit through a Canadian airport. The eTA is in force today (IRCC: 'You need an eTA and a valid passport to board your flight to Canada'). It is tied to your passport and, per IRCC, valid for up to five years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first; a new passport needs a new eTA. You do NOT need an eTA when arriving by car, bus, train or boat (including a cruise ship), but you still need a valid passport. With a valid eTA you can make repeated short visits, normally for up to six months at a time; the officer at the border decides the length of each stay. Apply only on the official Canada.ca site. IRCC's list names UK passport categories rather than 'United Kingdom' as a single entry, so check that your passport category is on the eTA list.
fee_notes: eTA fee CAD $7 per person (non-refundable), paid when applying.

conditions_text: IRCC lists Brazil as a visa-required country: a Brazilian passport holder needs a valid visitor visa unless the eTA exception below applies. IRCC also lists Brazil among the visa-required countries whose citizens MAY be eligible for an eTA instead of a visa, only if flying to or transiting a Canadian airport and only if you have held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years or currently hold a valid US non-immigrant visa (see the separate US-visa row). Arrivals by car, bus, train or boat always need a visitor visa.

Brazilian citizens who currently hold a valid US non-immigrant visa (or who have held a Canadian visitor visa in the past 10 years) may apply for a Canada eTA instead of a visitor visa. The eTA is in force today. The US non-immigrant visa must be valid on the day you apply for the eTA (it need not still be valid when you travel). The eTA is for travel BY AIR only (flying to or transiting a Canadian airport); you need a visitor visa to come by car, bus, train or boat, including a cruise ship. IRCC says the stay is normally up to six months, at the officer's discretion.
fee_notes: eTA fee CAD $7 per person (non-refundable).

conditions_text: Home Affairs lists the ETA (subclass 601) and the eVisitor (subclass 651) by eligible passport, and this passport is on neither list, so a Visitor visa (subclass 600), tourist stream, must be applied for and granted before travel (use the tourist stream for applications from overseas). Home Affairs states the visa is for tourists, business visitors or visiting family, for up to 12 months; the length of stay is set case by case on the visa grant letter and may be less than requested, and it can be granted for single or multiple entry. You must show you are a genuine visitor intending to stay temporarily, and that you have, or have access to, enough money for your stay. Health and character requirements apply. Check processing times on the Home Affairs processing-time guide before booking non-refundable travel. No fixed number of days applies: Home Affairs states the stay as a period set on your grant.
fee_notes: Visa application charge: the Home Affairs page does not state a figure (it is shown by their Visa Pricing Estimator); not recorded here.

conditions_text: Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601). Pre-travel online authorisation, in force today: the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601), applied for from outside Australia through the Australian ETA app (the Home Affairs page for the ETA was last updated 12 October 2026 and lists it as an open product). Home Affairs lists this passport as ETA-eligible. The ETA is valid for travel for 12 months or until the passport expires, whichever is shorter, with multiple entries; you can stay up to 3 months on each entry (entered here as 90 days). Tourism, visiting family or friends and some business visitor activities are allowed; you cannot work, and study or training is limited to 3 months in total. Catches from Home Affairs: you cannot apply with an Australian passport as a dual citizen; if you have a criminal conviction in any country, or have previously failed the health requirement, Home Affairs says to apply for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) instead; frequent or long stays may lead to questions about your travel purpose. Home Affairs suggests you do not make travel arrangements until the ETA is granted (most results are immediate, but not always).
fee_notes: Home Affairs: a service charge of AUD 20 applies to use the Australian ETA app, and there is no other charge payable for an ETA.

conditions_text: Pre-travel online authorisation, in force today, with two options for a British Citizen passport: the eVisitor (subclass 651; the Home Affairs page was last updated 8 September 2026) or the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601). Both list 'United Kingdom - British Citizen' as eligible; the ETA list also includes British National (Overseas), while the eVisitor excludes British National (Overseas), British Dependent Territories Citizen, British Overseas Citizen, British Protected Person and British Subject passports, and non-citizen passports. The eVisitor is applied for from outside Australia, is valid for travel for 12 months from the grant date with multiple entries, and allows up to 3 months on each entry (entered here as 90 days); if you want longer than 3 months at a time, apply for a different visa. The ETA is applied for through the Australian ETA app, with the same 3 months per entry. Neither allows work. Catches from Home Affairs: if you have a criminal conviction in any country, or have previously failed the health requirement, apply for a Visitor visa (subclass 600) instead; you cannot apply with an Australian passport as a dual citizen; you must have enough money to support yourself and to leave Australia.
fee_notes: eVisitor: Home Affairs states it is free. ETA: a service charge of AUD 20 applies to use the Australian ETA app, with no other charge.

Check processing times on the Home Affairs processing-time guide before booking non-refundable travel. No fixed number of days applies: Home Affairs states the stay as a period set on your grant.
fee_notes: Visa application charge: the Home Affairs page does not state a figure (it is shown by their Visa Pricing Estimator); not recorded here.

conditions_text: India is NOT on the DHA visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025): the list shows 90 days only for diplomatic, official and service passports, with the ordinary-passport column blank, so an ordinary Indian passport needs a visa or authorisation before travel. Two routes exist today. (1) ETA, in force now: South Africa's Electronic Travel Authorisation (official portal eta.dha.gov.za; launched officially 12 August 2026). India was one of the four original pilot nationalities (China, India, Indonesia, Mexico) named in the Minister's launch speech on gov.za, and the portal says holders of valid ordinary passports may apply online provided they will land at OR Tambo (Johannesburg), Cape Town, Lanseria or King Shaka airport. For visa-required travellers the ETA is issued as a port-of-entry visa (Section 10(a)); it is valid up to about 6 months, multiple entry, each stay up to 90 days, and the DHA says most outcomes arrive within 24 hours. The launch speech says the ETA will 'progressively become compulsory' for short stays from visa-required countries; no compulsory start date for India has been published, so treat it as the official online route and do not arrive without either an approved ETA or a visa. (2) Traditional visa: the South African High Commission in New Delhi states that all visa applications are lodged through VFS Global and that it does not accept applications directly; this route also covers arrival at any port other than the four ETA airports. Catches: the ETA FAQ says your passport must be valid for at least 7 months from your intended travel date, fees are non-refundable even if refused, an approved ETA does not guarantee entry, and a yellow-fever certificate is required if you arrive from a risk country. Carry return/onward ticket, accommodation and funds proof. Since 1 July 2026 all travellers must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration before entering or leaving.
fee_notes: The ETA fee amount is not stated on the DHA ETA pages checked; it is shown in the portal before you pay, and all ETA fees are non-refundable whether or not the application succeeds. VFS Global visa fees were not verified from an official page.

conditions_text: No visa needed: the Department of Home Affairs visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025, marked subject to change without notice) lists this nationality as exempt on ordinary passports for stays of up to 90 days, with no visa fee. Passport: the DHA says it must be valid for at least 30 days after the end of your intended visit and have at least one unused page for entry/departure endorsements; UK FCDO advises at least 2 blank pages, so carry 2. The Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) launched officially on 12 August 2026 at four airports (OR Tambo, Cape Town, Lanseria, King Shaka), but for visa-exempt travellers it is voluntary: the DHA ETA FAQ says visa-exempt travellers may travel without one and are processed under standard immigration procedures, so it is NOT required for this passport today. Catch: since 1 July 2026 every traveller entering or leaving South Africa must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration (a customs declaration, not a visa) before travelling. Carry a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, as the immigration officer can ask for these at the port of entry. A yellow-fever certificate is needed if you arrive from a yellow-fever-risk country. Special requirements apply for travellers aged 17 and under; check the DHA.

India is not on Korea's list of K-ETA-exempt countries (the Korean mission list names Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, the US, Guam, 15 European countries and Australia and New Zealand) and Indian passport holders must obtain a Korean visa in advance through the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr): fill in the e-Form online, print it and submit it in person at the KVAC-VFS visa application centre (the Chennai embassy page says Indian nationals 'must apply for Korean Visa and obtain it through the Visa Portal'). For tourism the usual category is the short-term tourist visa (C-3-9) described on Korean embassy pages. K-ETA is for visa-free nationalities and is not the route for Indian passport holders. The length of stay is set on the visa issued, so no fixed number of days applies. Catch: Korea runs a separate visa-free scheme for Jeju Island for nationals of visa-required countries who fly directly to Jeju from overseas (not via Seoul or Busan); the Korean mission notice (April 2026) lists 23 excluded nationalities and India is not among them. The Indian Embassy in Seoul (advisory of 24 February 2026) says the Jeju facility is for short-term tourism only, does not cover mainland Korea and does not guarantee entry: immigration officers at Jeju airport decide, and it advises carrying printed return ticket, hotel booking for the full stay, itinerary, proof of funds and a passport valid at least six months. A trip that continues to Seoul or Busan needs the visa.

No visa needed for tourism or business of up to 90 days (stated in the US State Department's South Korea advisory; travel.state.gov blocked automated fetching, so that figure was read through a search result rather than an opened page). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry, but US citizens are on the temporary K-ETA exemption list: the Korean consulate notice (Dallas, opened) says the exemption runs 1 January to 31 December 2026 (KST) and covers the US. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

British citizens can enter for up to 90 days for short-term business or tourism without a visa (UK FCDO). FCDO says you must have an onward or return ticket and that your passport must have an expiry date after you leave Korea. A K-ETA is usually required for visa-free entry but British nationals are temporarily exempt until 31 December 2026 (FCDO and the Korean mission exemption list). The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

Canadians can visit for tourism or business for up to 180 days without a visa (Global Affairs Canada; a Korean foreign-ministry mission page seen in search also describes six months for Canadians). Canada is the longest visa-free period of the eight passports. A passport valid beyond the expected departure date is required (transport companies may apply stricter rules). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry but Canadians are exempt until 31 December 2026 (Global Affairs Canada and the Korean mission exemption list). The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

Australian passport holders can visit as tourists for up to 90 days without a visa (Australian Government Smartraveller advice, read through a search result because the page timed out when fetched). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry, but Australia is on the temporary exemption list through 31 December 2026 (confirmed on the Korean mission list opened for this check). The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

German citizens (EU/Schengen nationals) can enter Korea without a visa for short stays that Germany's Auswaertiges Amt words as fewer than 90 days, with no employment. The passport must be valid on arrival with no minimum remaining validity required; a provisional passport is accepted but a Personalausweis (ID card) is not. A K-ETA is normally required but German citizens need none until 31 December 2026. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

Singapore passport holders do not need a visa for short-term entry; Singapore's MFA words this as under 90 days and the Korean embassy in Singapore describes the allowed stay as 90 days (both read through search results, not an opened page). The Korean embassy in Singapore states Singapore passport holders are exempt from K-ETA until 31 December 2026, and that there is no requirement on the passport's remaining validity as long as it stays valid throughout the stay in Korea. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

Brazilians do not need a visa for tourism, business, family visits or events of up to 90 days, but they must obtain a K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) before boarding, and it is in force today. Brazil is not on the K-ETA temporary exemption list (the list is Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, US, Guam, 15 European countries, Australia and New Zealand), so the requirement applies now. Brazil's foreign ministry (MRE) states the K-ETA is mandatory for stays of up to 90 days and that a visa is needed for stays of more than 90 days; the Korean embassy in Brazil says the K-ETA does not replace a visa, must be applied for at least 72 hours before travel on the official site k-eta.go.kr only (many look-alike sites charge more), and that a denied applicant cannot reapply successfully unless circumstances change significantly. The K-ETA guide on k-eta.go.kr states the fee is KRW 10,000 and processing is generally within 72 hours. The Korean embassy also says travellers who only visit Jeju on a direct flight do not need a K-ETA, but anyone planning to visit other regions needs one before entering Jeju.
fee_notes: K-ETA fee KRW 10,000 per the k-eta.go.kr guide; non-refundable per Korean mission notices.

conditions_text: Indian ordinary passports normally need a Serbian visa, but a nationality that needs a visa may enter without one with a valid UK visa, for a maximum of 90 days within a six-month period from the day of arrival, provided the documents remain valid for the entire stay. A still-valid visa in an old passport is accepted if the old passport is carried with the new one. If the document expires before the stay ends, apply for a C visa instead. The Serbian embassy in New Delhi's FAQ describes the visa as 'multiple entries'; the welcometoserbia page does not address entries. Different rules apply if you plan to work; longer stays need a D visa.

Indian nationals normally need a Mexican visa (India is on INM's list of countries that require one), but the INM page lists a valid, unexpired visa from Canada as an accepted alternative to a Mexican visa, alongside proof of permanent residence there. With one of these documents you may enter as a tourist or business visitor without a Mexican visa, still with a valid passport. By air there is no paper form: the digital FMM (FMMd) is generated at immigration and the officer stamps your passport with the days granted. By land you must carry a completed FMM (it can be filled in online beforehand or at the border). Visitors may not stay more than 180 days; the officer sets the actual days. No paid work. Confirm with the nearest Mexican consulate that your specific visa qualifies before booking.
fee_notes: The migratory fee for tourist entry is set each year in the Ley Federal de Derechos (2026 rates from 1 January 2026); the peso amount was not confirmed from a readable official page. Check the INM 2026 fee table.

The stay is up to 180 days within 365 days counted from first entry and is not extendable (Supreme Decree 006-2017-RE, in the Foreign Ministry's table of visa requirements). Check at the airline desk that your visa or residence document qualifies.

Indian passport holders with a valid UK visa or residence permit may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for 90 days in any 180-day period. Georgia's Ordinance No. 256 lists 50 qualifying countries (including the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan, Ireland, Israel, South Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland, Norway, Schengen states and several Gulf states); the visa or permit must be valid on the day you cross the border and you must be able to show it. The 2025 amendment that requires Gulf permits to be multiple-entry with at least a year's validity names 17 other nationalities, not India. Without such a visa or permit you need a Georgian e-visa. Since 1 January 2026 every tourist must also carry health and accident insurance covering the whole stay with at least 30,000 GEL of cover (printed or electronic, in English or Georgian; Georgian MFA notice).

Indian citizens need a Schengen short-stay visa for tourism in Germany (German Federal Foreign Office visa table). Apply through the German missions in India via VFS: every applicant needs an appointment and gives biometrics in person; applications can be lodged up to six months before the trip and the mission advises at least 15 calendar days (elsewhere at least three weeks) before travel. The mission aims to decide within 15 calendar days of lodging, which can extend up to 45 days in individual cases. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Requirements stated by the missions include a passport valid at least three months beyond departure from Schengen, issued within the previous 10 years, with at least two blank pages, and travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 valid across the Schengen area for the whole stay (German missions accept Indian policies only from approved Indian insurers). The missions also say that a long-stay visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen state allows travel in other Schengen states, still within the 90/180 limit. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 18 October 2026) says it is not in operation and no applications are collected. The EU Entry/Exit System registers non-EU travellers at the border (Germany: from 12 October 2025).
fee_notes: Schengen visa fee for adults EUR 90 / INR 9,900; minors aged 6 to 12 EUR 45 / INR 5,000; under 6 free (German missions in India fee page dated 1 October 2026, INR amounts 'subject to change without prior notice'). Paid at the end of the visa appointment; not refundable even if the visa is refused. VFS service fees are charged separately and are non-refundable; the page does not state their amount. Some applicants may qualify for a fee waiver, decided by the mission.

Indian passport holders need a Schengen short-stay visa (type C) for tourism in the Netherlands, applied for in advance at a VFS Global centre (NetherlandsWorldwide lists Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chandigarh, Chennai, Cochin, Hyderabad, Jalandhar, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Pune and New Delhi). Apply at least 15 days before travel and no more than 6 months before; you must attend in person with fingerprints (not needed if taken for a Schengen visa in the past 59 months), and book your own appointment. A Schengen visa allows a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. India is on the EU visa-required list (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu, checked 18 October 2026) says ETIAS is not in operation and no applications are collected. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) registers non-EU travellers (photo and fingerprints) at the border; NetherlandsWorldwide states the Netherlands has used EES since 12 October 2025.
fee_notes: Schengen visa fee EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children 6-11, free under 6 (NetherlandsWorldwide consular fee list for India, 2026; amounts may change). VFS Global service costs are charged separately; some applicants pay no fee.

Indian ordinary passport holders need a Schengen short-stay (category C) visa for Switzerland; SEM's nationality list shows a visa is required for stays of up to 90 days. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. The Swiss embassy in India says applications are lodged at VFS centres in India and decided by the Embassy of Switzerland in New Delhi (10 to 15 days after submission per its page, which is inconsistent on working vs calendar days), and may be submitted no earlier than 6 months before entry; SEM advises applying at least two months ahead. SEM's list exempts third-country nationals holding both a valid residence permit issued by a Schengen state (or a valid type D visa) and a recognised travel document, so that holder needs no short-stay visa (Schengen residence is not modelled as a held-document cascade in this app). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the official ETIAS website says it is not in operation).
fee_notes: Visa fee EUR 90 for adults and EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 12 (SEM FAQ); not refunded if refused or withdrawn. The external service provider (VFS) charges its own additional service fee; amount not confirmed.

conditions_text: Switzerland is in the Schengen area but not in the EU. No visa is needed for visits of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. Per the Swiss State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), your passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after your intended departure from the Schengen area. Border officers can ask for proof of the purpose of the stay; SEM's FAQ says travellers staying at their own expense must be able to show means of at least CHF 100 per day. The EU Entry/Exit System registers non-EU travellers at the Schengen border; SEM says it has been introduced gradually since October 2025. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, EUR 20) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) states it is currently not in operation, no applications are collected, and the EU will announce the start date several months before launch; SEM says travellers currently need do nothing. Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change. SEM's list notes that gainful work in construction, catering and hotel services, cleaning, security and erotic services, or other work over 8 days in a calendar year, needs a visa (a visit as a tourist does not).

Switzerland is in the Schengen area but not in the EU, so this is not EU-internal freedom of movement. SEM states that citizens of an EU or EFTA state need no visa to enter Switzerland, and SEM's nationality list shows no visa requirement for Germany. German citizens can enter with a valid recognised identity document: a passport or a valid national identity card (Personalausweis); SEM's list also accepts the extra documents in its note DEU-1 (for example a passport or identity card expired for less than one year, or a valid temporary Personalausweis). The 3-months-beyond-departure and 10-year-issue passport rules SEM applies to third-country nationals are not applied to you. For a stay over 90 days the Swiss foreign ministry says you need an authorisation from the migration authority of the canton concerned; this row covers visits only. No ETIAS applies to EU citizens (and ETIAS is in any case not in operation today).

Indian passport holders are on the EU list of nationalities that need a visa to cross the Schengen external border (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806). For tourism a Schengen short-stay (Type C) visa must be applied for in advance, in practice through the Austrian embassy or its appointed application centre, with supporting documents; Austria's foreign ministry says nationals of visa-required countries need a visa for stays of up to six months in principle. A short-stay visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Holders of a Schengen residence permit or national long-stay (D) visa do not need a short-stay visa and are exempt from EES registration (bmi.gv.at). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the European Commission ETIAS page says it is not in operation).

No visa needed for short stays in Austria (Schengen area) of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (stated on the UK FCDO Austria page; same Schengen Borders Code rule for all visa-exempt travellers). Border officers may ask for proof of accommodation, travel insurance, a return or onward ticket and enough money for the stay. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) registers photo and fingerprints of non-EU visitors on entry; Austria's interior ministry (bmi.gv.at) says in Austria it applies at the international airports and that full operation at all Schengen external borders began 10 April 2026. Refusing biometrics can mean refused entry. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers) is NOT in force today: the European Commission ETIAS page says it is not in operation and no applications are being collected, and that a start date will be announced several months before launch (that page is dated 6 October 2025; I found no later official start date). Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking.

India is on the Irish Immigration Service's Visa Required Nationalities list (list as published by the Irish Embassy in Belgium via assets.ireland.ie, last updated 12 May 2025), so Indian passport holders must obtain an Irish short stay 'C' visa before travelling, even for tourism. A visa does not guarantee entry, and the visa's validity dates govern when you may travel, not how long you may stay: the Immigration Officer at the port of entry sets the stay, and a 'C' visa covers visits of 90 days or less. Ireland is not in Schengen, so a Schengen visa is not accepted, and UK visas are also not valid for Ireland except in limited cases under the Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme. Indian nationals living in India may be eligible for the British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS), a single visa valid for short stays in both Ireland and the UK; you must enter the country that issued the visa first. Ireland has no ETA for visitors, so none is in force; the visa is the pre-travel requirement. Check the Irish Immigration Service (irishimmigration.ie) for the application steps, which are not covered here.

USA passport holders are on the Irish Immigration Service's list of Non-Visa Required Nationalities (list as published by the Irish Embassy in Belgium via assets.ireland.ie, last updated 12 May 2025), so no visa is needed for a visit. Visa-exempt nationals are still subject to immigration control on arrival: an Immigration Officer decides whether to admit you and for how long (the entry stamp sets your permitted stay), and visits are limited to 90 days; longer stays need permission beyond a visitor visit (a 'D' visa applied for before travel, per the Irish Government's visas page at api.ireland.ie). Ireland has no ETA, so a US passport holder (unlike for the UK) needs no online authorisation to enter the Republic. Ireland (the Republic) has no ETA or pre-travel online authorisation for visitors: the Irish pages consulted (api.ireland.ie visas page, Canada's travel advice) mention none, so nothing is in force today. Ireland is not in Schengen, so a Schengen visa or ETIAS does not apply. The UK ETA is a separate scheme for the UK (including Northern Ireland) and is not needed for the Republic.

Under the Common Travel Area, British citizens do not need a visa to visit, live, work or study in Ireland, and there is no fixed 90-day cap. UK FCDO says British nationals are not legally required to show a passport to enter Ireland, but you should carry one to prove identity, Irish immigration officers can ask for proof of British nationality, and some airlines and ferry operators require passport-only ID, so check with your carrier. This applies to holders of a full British citizen passport; other categories of UK passport should check with the Irish Embassy in the UK. Ireland is in the EU but not Schengen, and has no ETA for visitors, so none is in force. This row cites UK FCDO as the Irish immigration pages could not be fetched in full.

Global Affairs Canada says Canadian citizens do not need a tourist or business visa for stays up to 90 days. Your passport must be valid for the entire expected length of your stay (your carrier may apply stricter validity rules), and customs or immigration officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds; entry can be refused without them. Canada is also on the Irish Immigration Service's Non-Visa Required list. The Immigration Officer at the border decides whether to admit you and for how long, up to 90 days. Ireland has no ETA for visitors, so none is in force (Global Affairs Canada's page mentions none). The UK ETA is a separate scheme for the UK, including Northern Ireland, and is not needed for the Republic. This row cites Global Affairs Canada as a fallback because irishimmigration.ie pages could not be fetched in full.

A German national intending to live or work in Ireland should check registration rules with the Irish authorities.

Indian passport holders need a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa for Croatia: India is on the list of countries whose nationals must have a visa to cross the external borders of the EU (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806). Croatia has applied the Schengen rules in full since 1 January 2023 and issues Schengen visas at its missions; the Croatian foreign ministry's India page says applications can also be submitted at VFS centres in New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Croatia's foreign ministry (mvep.gov.hr, page for US citizens) says the passport must expire no less than three months after the scheduled departure from Croatia and have been issued within the last 10 years. Visa-holders are not guaranteed entry and may be asked at the border for accommodation, funds and a return ticket. The accommodation provider must register your arrival with the police within 48 hours (UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada state this for all visitors). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities (the official ETIAS website describes it as for visa-exempt travellers) and is NOT in force today: that site (checked 18 October 2026) states it is currently not in operation and collects no applications. Non-EU travellers are also registered in the EU Entry/Exit System at the border.
fee_notes: Visa fee amount not confirmed from an official Croatian page opened for this record (the Croatian foreign ministry's India page states no fee); check with the Croatian mission or VFS before applying.

When it starts the same site lists a EUR 20 fee. Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now.

EU freedom of movement: German citizens do not need a visa for Croatia. The Croatian e-government portal (gov.hr) states that EEA nationals may stay in Croatia for up to three months from entry with a valid travel document or identity card and need not register a short stay; stays over three months must be registered with the police administration within eight days after the three months end (EUR 20 fine for late registration). The EU Entry/Exit System applies only to non-EU nationals and ETIAS is for visa-exempt non-EU travellers (and is not in operation today), so neither affects German citizens.

Indian citizens are on the Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of states whose citizens need a visa to travel to the Schengen area. For tourism, apply for a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa in advance, in person at a Czech consulate or visa centre in your consular district; applications are not accepted at the border or inside Czechia. The Czech ministry's visa-centre page lists VFS centres in India at Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chandigarh, Chennai, Goa, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jalandhar, Kochi, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi and Pune. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area; proof of accommodation, travel medical insurance and proof of funds are required with the application. Passport validity: at least 3 months beyond departure from Schengen and issued within the previous 10 years (UK FCDO Schengen rule, fallback; the Czech pages fetched did not state it). ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the European Commission says it is 'currently not in operation'). The EU Entry/Exit System has been fully operational since 10 April 2026. I did not confirm from an official page whether the Czech post in New Delhi or VFS is the correct office for each Indian state, or the VFS service fee: check the Czech embassy and VFS before booking.
fee_notes: Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs fee schedule: Schengen visa EUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for ages 6-11 (may be waived at consulate discretion), free under 6. The fee is non-refundable if refused. A VFS service fee is separate and not stated on the Czech page.

Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area (stated on the UK FCDO Czech Republic entry page, used here as a fallback because the Czech ministry pages fetched did not state a validity period; the Schengen-wide rule). Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Overstaying can lead to an entry ban of up to 3 years (UK FCDO). The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) has been fully operational since 10 April 2026 and replaces manual passport stamping; first entry may involve fingerprints and a photo (Czech MFA EES page). Do not pay any website claiming to issue ETIAS now; check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change.

EU freedom of movement: German citizens can enter and travel in Czechia with either a valid passport or a valid national identity card (the document must be valid on the day of travel). No visa, no ETIAS and no EES registration apply to EU citizens.

Indian nationals are on the list of nationalities that need a visa to cross the Schengen external border (Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which Iceland applies as a Schengen state). A Schengen short-stay visa must be obtained in advance for tourism; it allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area. Iceland's island.is entry-requirements page says the visa condition does not apply to a person who holds a residence permit from another EEA/EFTA country. Visa services in Iceland moved from the Directorate of Immigration to the Ministry for Foreign Affairs under Visa Act No. 37/2026 (island.is notice dated 13 May 2026). Passport must be issued within the previous 10 years and valid at least 3 months beyond your intended departure; you must also show the purpose of the visit and enough money for the stay and the return. ETIAS does not apply to visa-required nationalities and is not in force today (the official ETIAS website says it is not in operation). Fee and processing time not verified from an official page opened for this row; check with the Icelandic embassy in New Delhi or the Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

No visa needed for short stays in Iceland (a Schengen state) of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across all Schengen countries combined. Passport must have been issued within the previous 10 years and be valid for at least 3 months beyond the date you intend to leave the Schengen area. Iceland's official entry-requirements page (island.is) says you must be able to state the purpose of your visit and show enough money for your stay and for your return, so carry a return or onward ticket and proof of funds. Longer stays need an Icelandic residence permit. The EU Entry/Exit System registers face and fingerprints at the Schengen border on first entry. ETIAS (the EU online travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers, which will cover Iceland) is NOT in force today: the official ETIAS website (travel-europe.europa.eu) states it is currently not in operation, no applications are collected, and the start date will be announced several months before launch. Do not pay any website that claims to issue ETIAS now. Check travel-europe.europa.eu before booking, because this is expected to change.

Iceland is in the Schengen area and the EEA but not the EU, so German citizens enter under the EEA Agreement's free movement of persons (not EU law directly). No visa and no stay limit for a visit. Iceland's island.is entry-requirements page says EEA/EFTA citizens must carry a valid travel document or identity card accepted for border crossing, valid beyond their stay; a German passport or national ID card therefore works (airlines may apply their own document rules). Registration with Registers Iceland is required if you stay longer than three months (the island.is registration page for EEA/EFTA nationals says three months; the entry-requirements page says six, so register promptly if staying long). ETIAS does not apply to EU/EEA citizens and is not in force today for anyone.
