India is on ICA's list of 34 countries and places whose travel documents need a valid Singapore entry visa; ICA does not accept visa applications at immigration counters. Apply before travel: online through ICA's e-Service via a Singapore local contact or strategic partner, or at the Singapore High Commission in New Delhi through its authorised visa agents (ICA says apply within 30 days before arrival). ICA's India page asks for Form 14A, a photo taken in the last 3 months and a passport biodata page valid at least 6 months from entry (Form V39A may be requested); the High Commission says a flight ticket is not needed before applying and that processing is generally 3 to 5 working days. A visa does not guarantee entry, and the length of stay is set by the Visit Pass issued at the checkpoint, not by the visa's validity (neither ICA nor the High Commission gives a stay figure). Catch: there is no general concession for Indians who hold other countries' visas; the only documented one is the 96-hour transit facility (see the held-document rules). Indians without a Singapore visa who are not eligible for that facility will not be allowed to enter. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: ICA's India page lists S$30 (non-refundable, paid online by Visa or MasterCard); the High Commission's page lists an INR 2,100 non-refundable processing fee and says authorised agents may add Rs.1,300. ICA's India page is marked last updated 2 March 2024, so confirm the amount when applying.

conditions_text: US passport holders (regular, official and diplomatic) do not need a visa to enter Singapore for business or social visits, per the Singapore Embassy in Washington. The length of stay is decided by immigration officers at entry (it is not tied to a visa), so check the stay you are granted; the Embassy page gives no number of days. Catch: you still must meet ICA's entry requirements: proof of onward travel, sufficient funds and a passport with 6 months' validity; Singapore also bans vapes and e-cigarettes. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity (ICA); Canada's GAC counts it from the date you enter, while the Singapore MFA checklist words it as 6 months at the time of departure, so plan on 6 months remaining at departure to satisfy both. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The SG Arrival Card is free.

conditions_text: UK FCDO says British citizens can visit Singapore without a visa for tourism or business. The permitted stay is at the immigration officer's discretion and for British citizens is 'normally between 30 and 90 days', so no fixed number is given here. Catch: overstaying can bring fines, imprisonment, caning or deportation; your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity (ICA); Canada's GAC counts it from the date you enter, while the Singapore MFA checklist words it as 6 months at the time of departure, so plan on 6 months remaining at departure to satisfy both. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The SG Arrival Card is free.

conditions_text: Global Affairs Canada says a tourist visa is not required for stays of up to 30 days, and that ICA may approve an extension in certain circumstances. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date you enter (also for transit passengers). Catch: since 30 January 2026 Singapore has enforced a No-Boarding Directive for travellers with insufficient passport validity, among other grounds, and customs officials may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The SG Arrival Card is free.

conditions_text: Smartraveller (DFAT) states that Australian passport holders do not require a visa to enter Singapore. The length of stay is set by the Visit Pass granted at the checkpoint (ICA); the pages checked give no number of days, so none is stated here. Catch: ICA asks for sufficient cash and proof of onward travel, and Smartraveller warns that vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to bring in even in transit. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity (ICA); Canada's GAC counts it from the date you enter, while the Singapore MFA checklist words it as 6 months at the time of departure, so plan on 6 months remaining at departure to satisfy both. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The SG Arrival Card is free; Smartraveller warns of scam sites that charge for it.

conditions_text: Germany's Foreign Office says German citizens need no visa for stays of up to 90 days and receive a 90-day stay permission on entry. Only a passport, provisional passport or children's passport is accepted (not the national ID card), and it must be valid at least 6 months on entry with free pages. Catch: longer stays need a separate pass (ICA explains the categories). Being an EU citizen gives no Schengen-style freedom of movement in Singapore. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The SG Arrival Card is free.

conditions_text: Brazil is not on ICA's list of 34 countries and places whose travel documents need a Singapore visa, so Brazilian passport holders enter without a visa. A March 2026 notice from the Brazilian Embassy in Singapore refers to Brazilians who entered visa-free for up to 30 days and says to ask ICA (ica.gov.sg) for an extension before the stay expires. ICA's own pages give no stay figure for visa-exempt nationals (the Visit Pass granted at the checkpoint sets it), so treat 30 days as the figure to plan on and check the Visit Pass you are given. Catch: ICA asks for sufficient cash and proof of onward travel. Passport must have at least 6 months' validity (ICA); Canada's GAC counts it from the date you enter, while the Singapore MFA checklist words it as 6 months at the time of departure, so plan on 6 months remaining at departure to satisfy both. Everyone entering must submit the free SG Arrival Card (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival, counting the day of arrival; ICA says it is free and not a visa.
fee_notes: No visa fee. ICA charges S$40 for an extension that takes the stay to 90 days or more from entry.

conditions_text: Indian citizens are currently exempt from the Malaysian visa for up to 30 days for business, tourism, social or transit purposes. The Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi states the waiver runs until 31 December 2026, and the Immigration Department's visa-requirement page carries the same end date (it lists India as visa-required with the footnote 'visa exempts until 31st December 2026'). Catch: the waiver has a fixed end date and no extension beyond 31 December 2026 was found, so anyone travelling on or after 1 January 2027 must re-check before booking. The High Commission lists the conditions: passport valid for at least six months, confirmed return flight ticket, confirmed hotel booking, and compulsory online submission of the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) three days before arrival. The old eNTRI scheme (15-day registration) is not needed under the waiver; the Immigration Department's eNTRI page only describes the 2017-18 programme. The waiver covers visits only: work or study needs a visa arranged beforehand.
fee_notes: No visa fee under the waiver. No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: US citizens do not need a visa to visit Malaysia for business or social reasons if the stay is 90 days or less, per the Consulate General of Malaysia in Los Angeles. Everyone entering must complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within three days before arrival. Malaysia's general entry conditions require a passport valid for more than six months and sufficient funds, and immigration may ask to see a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation. Work, study or a stay over 90 days needs a visa arranged beforehand. The Los Angeles page is undated; the US State Department page that confirms the same rule could not be opened (blocked to automated access).
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: British citizens do not need a visa for tourism and will normally be allowed to stay 90 days on arrival, per UK FCDO (used because the Malaysian Immigration Department's visa-requirement page lists the United Kingdom as visa-exempt but states no length of stay). Passport must be valid for at least six months after the arrival date, undamaged, with no missing pages. FCDO says you must submit the online arrival card (the MDAC) before travelling; airlines may ask to see it at check-in. Longer stays or non-tourist purposes (work, study) need a visa applied for before travel.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: Canadian citizens do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 90 days, per Global Affairs Canada (page last updated 9 October 2026). The passport must be valid for at least six months beyond the date you expect to leave Malaysia. A Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) must be completed, up to three days before arrival. For longer stays you must apply for an extension at a Malaysian Immigration office.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: Australians can in most circumstances get a 90-day tourist pass on arrival with no prior visa, per Smartraveller (updated 2 October 2026). You must complete a Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) before you arrive, submitted through the Malaysian Immigration website; for the auto gates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (T1 and T2) you also need a passport valid at least six months and the MDAC submitted three days before arrival. Smartraveller warns that entry conditions can change at short notice and advises confirming with a Malaysian High Commission or consulate.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: German citizens need no visa for entry and a stay of up to three months without gainful employment, per the German Foreign Office (Auswaertiges Amt; page updated October 2026). Travel documents must be valid six months beyond entry, have free pages and be undamaged. The online Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is required within three days before entry. Immigration may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of booked accommodation. Catch: the Foreign Office says that on entering the East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak a separate pass is issued, usually valid 90 days.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: Singapore citizens do not require a visa to enter Malaysia for up to 30 days, per Singapore's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (the Malaysian Immigration Department's page says visas are not required for Singapore nationals even beyond one month, so 30 days is the conservative figure). Singapore passports must be valid for more than six months at entry. Singapore passport holders are exempt from the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card at all entry points; those who want to enrol fingerprints for e-gate clearance on later entries should submit the MDAC three days before arrival. Singaporeans may need a visa for onward travel from Malaysia to a third country.
fee_notes: No visa fee. No MDAC needed for Singapore passport holders.

conditions_text: Brazilian citizens on a national passport do not need a visa for a social or business stay of up to 90 days, per the Embassy of Malaysia in Brasilia; other purposes or longer stays need a visa obtained before departure. Catch: Brazil's embassy in Kuala Lumpur (gov.br/mre) states that travellers with a Brazilian passport or coming from Brazil may enter Malaysia only with an original International Certificate of Vaccination showing yellow fever vaccination at least ten days before travel, even if only in transit. It also says travellers must complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) before arrival. Passport must be valid for more than six months. The Brasilia embassy page is undated.
fee_notes: No visa fee. The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) is free; only use the official Immigration Department site (imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main) because look-alike sites charge.

conditions_text: US citizens are on Taiwan's visa-exempt list for stays of up to 90 days (Bureau of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Conditions on the BOCA visa-exempt page: a regular passport with at least six months' remaining validity on the date of entry, a confirmed return or onward air/sea ticket (or a visa for the next destination) and a confirmed seat reservation for departure. The stay starts the day after arrival and a visa-exempt stay cannot be extended (conversion to a visa-based stay is allowed only in limited cases such as force majeure). An online immigration arrival card must be completed within seven days before arriving. BOCA notes that US nationals are the one group allowed to use an emergency passport under the visa exemption.

British citizens are on Taiwan's visa-exempt list for stays of up to 90 days; BOCA says only British Citizen passport holders qualify (other British nationality types are not covered by this entry). An online immigration arrival card must be completed within seven days before arriving. BOCA also says UK and Canadian passport holders may extend the 90-day stay up to 180 days under a separate notice; check that notice before relying on it.

Brazil is not on Taiwan's visa-exempt list (BOCA lists Brazil in neither the 90-day, 30-day nor 14-day group) and Brazil is not among the nationalities eligible for Taiwan's eVisa, so Brazilian passport holders apply for a visitor visa in advance at the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in Brazil (Sao Paulo or Brasilia). The office's tourist-visa page asks for a signed online form, a passport valid for at least six months, two 3x4 photos, a flight ticket copy and hotel reservation, bank statements or payslips for the last three months and the income tax return. The office page does not state the permitted length of stay, so none is given here. Catch: the office pages are undated and processing times on them are inconsistent (7 versus up to 10 working days), so confirm requirements with the office before booking.
fee_notes: The office's tourism-visa page lists R$185 (single entry) and R$370 (multiple entry), with urgent processing R$92 / R$185 extra, but the page is undated and another São Paulo page shows different figures, so the current fee is not confirmed.

conditions_text: India is not on Taiwan's visa-exempt list and is not a general eVisa nationality (BOCA's eVisa page lists India only for business visitors recommended by Taiwan External Trade Development Council overseas offices and for group tourists on designated high-end tour programmes). An ordinary Indian passport holder without a qualifying foreign visa normally applies for a visitor (tourism) visa in person at the Taipei Economic and Cultural Center in India (or its Chennai office): the TECC India tourism-visa page lists a signed online form, a request letter, a day-by-day itinerary, confirmed return ticket and hotel booking, an employer NOC, photos, a passport valid for more than 6 months, financial proof, Form 16 or ITR, and three months of bank statements, submitted in person only. The page does not state the permitted stay, so none is given. Catch: Indians who hold a qualifying visa or residence card from another country can instead get the online Travel Authorization Certificate (see the held-document rows).
fee_notes: Visa fee not stated on the TECC India tourism-visa page (it links to a separate fee page that was not read).

conditions_text: Indian regular-passport holders who hold a qualifying document from the USA can apply online for the ROC (Taiwan) Travel Authorization Certificate (TAC, the National Immigration Agency's online authorisation, in force today) instead of applying for a visa. Qualifying document: a valid resident or permanent resident card, a valid entry visa (an e-visa must be printed), or a resident card or visa that expired less than 10 years before arrival, from Australia, Canada, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, a Schengen country, the UK or the US (this row applies if yours is from the USA; the other countries have their own rows or are named here, and Schengen is not modelled as a held-document country). Work permits do not count and visas marked VOID or CANCELLED are ineligible. Also required: a passport valid at least six months from arrival, an onward or return air/boat ticket, and never having worked in Taiwan as a blue-collar worker. An approved certificate is valid for 90 days with multiple entries; each stay is up to 30 days from the day after arrival (BOCA and the TECC India notice; an older TECC India page says 14 days and 6 entries per calendar year, so check at application). Print the certificate and carry the qualifying document; without it you will not be admitted. Apply at least seven days before a current certificate expires to renew. Complete the online arrival card before each entry.
fee_notes: BOCA and the TECC India pages do not state a fee for the Travel Authorization Certificate.

Qualifying document: a valid resident or permanent resident card, a valid entry visa (an e-visa must be printed), or a resident card or visa that expired less than 10 years before arrival, from Australia, Canada, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, a Schengen country, the UK or the US (this row applies if yours is from Japan; the other countries have their own rows or are named here, and Schengen is not modelled as a held-document country). Work permits do not count and visas marked VOID or CANCELLED are ineligible. Also required: a passport valid at least six months from arrival, an onward or return air/boat ticket, and never having worked in Taiwan as a blue-collar worker. An approved certificate is valid for 90 days with multiple entries; each stay is up to 30 days from the day after arrival (BOCA and the TECC India notice; an older TECC India page says 14 days and 6 entries per calendar year, so check at application). Print the certificate and carry the qualifying document; without it you will not be admitted. Apply at least seven days before a current certificate expires to renew. Complete the online arrival card before each entry.
fee_notes: BOCA and the TECC India pages do not state a fee for the Travel Authorization Certificate.

conditions_text: India's e-Tourist visa (e-Visa, applied for online at indianvisaonline.gov.in) is in force today and is the pre-travel requirement; United States of America is on the portal's list of eligible countries. Categories on the portal: 30-day (multiple entry per the portal; non-extendable and non-convertible; the portal FAQ counts the 30 days from first arrival, which must fall inside the ETA's validity dates), 1-year (365 days from the date the ETA is granted, multiple entry) and 5-year (five years from the date granted, multiple entry); a separate 6-month e-T2 category is also listed. Per-visit stay on the 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist visas: continuous stay during each visit shall not exceed 180 days for USA nationals (the default for other nationalities is 90 days). Catch: for the 1-year and 5-year categories the portal also says total stay in India in one calendar year must not exceed 180 days, so max_stay_days is the per-visit ceiling and a 30-day visa allows only 30 days. The passport must be valid at least six months when you apply and have at least two blank pages; apply at least 4 days before arrival and up to 120 days ahead (fees must be paid at least 4 days before travel); entry only via the designated airports and seaports; not valid for Protected, Restricted or Cantonment Areas without separate permission. A separate e-Arrival card can be filed within 72 hours before arrival and is not a visa. The per-visit stay rule (90 days, 180 for USA, UK, Canada and Japan) is from the Embassy of India, Muscat e-Visa page (indemb-oman.gov.in/page/electronic-visa-issued-by-government-of-india-through-e-visa-portal/, updated 15 October 2026), not from the portal page cited here.
fee_notes: Official e-Tourist fee table dated 8 September 2026 (US$, USA): 30-day visa $10 if applying for April to June, $25 for July to March; 1-year $40; 5-year $160. A 3% bank charge is added; fees are non-refundable and the portal charges no express fee (indianvisaonline.gov.in/evisa/images/Etourist_fee_final.pdf).

conditions_text: India is not on China's unilateral visa-free list (NIA list compiled as of 17 February 2026) or its mutual visa-exemption list, and is not among the 57 nationalities eligible for the 240-hour visa-free transit scheme (NIA page of 20 August 2026), so Indian ordinary-passport holders need a Chinese visa obtained before travel; for tourism this is the L visa, applied for through the Chinese Embassy or consulates in India and their visa application centres, and the embassy may ask for supporting documents or an interview. The stay length is set on the visa itself. Foreign visitors are also asked to complete China's arrival card (online from 20 November 2025, or on arrival).
fee_notes: Chinese Embassy in India FAQ lists INR 2,900 for a single-entry visa, 4,400 double-entry, 5,900 six-month multiple-entry, 8,800 multiple-entry over one year, plus INR 1,800 if express is requested, excluding visa-centre service fees. The page does not mention the reduced-fee notice; check the current schedule before paying.

conditions_text: The United States is not on China's unilateral visa-free list (NIA list compiled as of 17 February 2026) and has no mutual visa-exemption agreement with China, so US ordinary-passport holders need a Chinese visa before travel; for tourism this is the L visa, applied for through the Chinese Embassy or Consulates-General in the US. The one exception is the 240-hour visa-free transit scheme, which the NIA page of 20 August 2026 says covers US nationals: you must be passing through China to a third country or region with a confirmed onward ticket and enter at one of 65 designated ports, and you may stay up to 10 days in the permitted area. A flight from the US that continues to a third country qualifies; a round trip that returns to the US does not. Foreign visitors are also asked to complete China's arrival card (online from 20 November 2025, or on arrival).
fee_notes: The Chinese Consulate-General in New York notice (30 December 2025) says reduced visa fees continue until 31 December 2026 and shows US$140 for a single-entry visa for US citizens; the other rows of its table were not clearly readable, so confirm other entry types with the visa office.

conditions_text: Visa-free entry for up to 30 days for business, tourism, visiting relatives or friends, exchange visits or transit, for holders of an ordinary passport. This is a unilateral exemption by China, not a treaty right: the National Immigration Administration list (compiled as of 17 February 2026) names the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland among the 50 countries; the Chinese Embassy in the UK notice of 15 February 2026 gives the UK window as 00:00 on 17 February 2026 to 24:00 on 31 December 2026, and states no end date, while Chinese embassy notices set the exemption to run until 24:00 Beijing time on 31 December 2026. As of 18 October 2026 no extension beyond that date was found, so check the NIA or Chinese embassy before booking any trip that enters China after 31 December 2026. The 30 days count from 00:00 on the day after entry. Work, study, journalism and stays over 30 days need the proper visa first. All foreign visitors, including visa-free ones, are asked to complete China's arrival card; since 20 November 2025 it can be filled in online before travel (NIA website, the NIA 12367 app, or a WeChat/Alipay mini-program), and anyone who has not can do it at the immigration inspection site by QR code, port kiosk or paper card.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-free entry.

conditions_text: Indian citizens do not need a visa to enter Nepal (Nepal Department of Immigration; this reflects the long-standing India-Nepal open-border arrangement under the India-Nepal treaty arrangement, which the official pages do not name). No maximum length of stay is stated for Indian citizens on the official pages, so max_stay_days is left null. At Tribhuvan International Airport, immigration accepts a passport or a Voter ID card as proof of Indian nationality. Minors need a birth certificate, and children under 18 travelling with parents can use a school identity card. A machine-readable passport is mandatory for all travellers at the airport. The Embassy of India in Kathmandu is stricter for air travel between India and Nepal: it says only two documents are valid, a valid Indian passport or an original Election Commission of India Voter ID card with photograph. A downloaded or printed Voter ID is not accepted, and Aadhaar, PAN card, driving licence and embassy registration are not accepted as travel documents. Carry the passport or original Voter ID, not Aadhaar. The embassy page covers air travel only; for land crossings it does not state the accepted documents, so carry a passport or original Voter ID there too and check before crossing.
fee_notes: No visa and no visa fee for Indian citizens (DoI: Indian citizens do not require a visa to enter Nepal).

conditions_text: US citizens may take the ordinary tourist visa below. DoI also lists a separate reciprocity tourist visa for US citizens: 5-year validity, up to 180 days stay per year, fee USD 160, applied for with the Department of Immigration with a bank statement (minimum USD 10,000), health insurance certificate and police report. Foreign nationals arriving after 16 September 2025 must also register through the NepaliPort website or app on arrival (Global Affairs Canada). Nepal issues tourist visas on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu) and other designated entry points, or in advance through the Department of Immigration's online eVisa/ETA portal or a Nepalese embassy. The Department of Immigration (DoI) page lists three tourist visa lengths: 15, 30 or 90 days from the date of entry. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months (DoI: before the date of travel; the UK FCDO words it as 6 months after the date of entry); Tribhuvan airport immigration also requires a machine-readable passport. A visa must be used within 6 months of its issue date, cannot be withdrawn once issued, and the fee is non-refundable. Tourist visas can be extended inside Nepal (DoI offices in Kathmandu and Pokhara) up to a combined 150 days per visa year (1 January to 31 December). The DoI list of nationalities that cannot get a visa on arrival (Nigeria, Ghana, Zimbabwe, Swaziland, Cameroon, Somalia, Liberia, Ethiopia, Iraq, Palestine, Afghanistan, Syria) does not include this passport.
fee_notes: DoI tourist visa fees (USD): 15 days USD 30, 30 days USD 50, 90 days USD 125. Extension USD 3 per day with a 15-day minimum; overstay fine USD 5 per day; DoI also lists an additional USD 25 re-entry fee (the page calls the visas multiple-entry and does not reconcile the two). Children under 10 are eligible for a free visa of up to 30 days (the DoI page says all nationalities except US citizens); the 90-day visa is always charged. DoI says to pay in USD online on the eVisa portal; cash in USD at the airport is the usual fallback. The free under-10 visa does not apply to US citizens. Reciprocity visa: USD 160 for 5 years.

conditions_text: A tourist visa is required. Get the single-entry Tourist (Visa T) e-Visa online at evisa.gov.kh before you go (the portal says processing takes 3 business days and the visa is valid for 3 months from issue), or buy a tourist visa on arrival at international airports and major land crossings. The visa allows a 30-day stay, counted from the date of entry, and can be extended once (by up to one month) inside Cambodia. Catch 1: the e-Visa portal says the passport must have more than six months' validity at entry; Global Affairs Canada and UK FCDO also state six months. Catch 2: separately from the visa, every air traveller must complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival Card (arrival.gov.kh) within 7 days before arrival. Catch 3: the e-Visa is accepted only at listed ports (Techo International, Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports; Bavet and Tropaeng Kreal land crossings); Cham Yeam and Poipet are marked temporarily closed for e-Visa entry, and all land crossings with Thailand are closed as of October 2026 (Smartraveller). Catch 4: Canada's advisory says an onward or return ticket and proof of funds are required. Overstaying is fined and can block departure. The tourism ministry's site notes that from 3 October 2026 visa issuance is being fully digitalised and physical visa stickers discontinued, so expect a printed or digital e-Visa certificate rather than a sticker.
fee_notes: e-Visa (Visa T, single entry): USD 30 per the official evisa.gov.kh portal (checked 18 Oct 2026). Tourist visa on arrival: US$30, paid in US dollars, per the Ministry of Tourism's visa page (tourismcambodia.com, last updated Sept 2025; the portal itself prices only the e-Visa). Extension of a tourist visa and overstay fine (US$10 per day per the same tourism page) were not confirmed on a government immigration page. e-Arrival Card is free.

conditions_text: Singapore citizens are visa-free for tourism for up to 30 days. Cambodia's official e-Visa portal lists Singapore among the ASEAN nationalities that do not need the tourist visa, and the Singapore MFA states 'visa-free entry for up to 30 days' for tourists (page updated 17 October 2026). Note: the 14-day figure is the ASEAN framework default and applies to Cambodia's lists for other nationalities (for example Brunei), not Singapore; the Cambodian embassy exemption table (updated 2019) also shows 30 days for Singapore regular passports. Catch 1: air travellers must complete the free Cambodia e-Arrival Card (arrival.gov.kh) within 7 days before arrival. Catch 2: UK FCDO and Canada state six months' passport validity, and Canada states an onward or return ticket and proof of funds are required. Catch 3: all land crossings with Thailand are closed as of October 2026. Staying beyond 30 days needs a visa; confirm with the Royal Embassy of Cambodia in Singapore.
fee_notes: No visa fee for visa-free entry. The e-Arrival Card is free (arrival.gov.kh).

conditions_text: India is not on Immigration New Zealand's visa waiver list, so a Visitor Visa must be applied for and granted before you travel (INZ states visitor visa applications must be made online from 1 October 2026). INZ states a visitor can stay up to 9 months in an 18-month period, with multiple-entry visas capped at 6 months in any 12 months; the actual stay is set on the visa you are granted, so no fixed number of days applies here. Conditions stated by INZ: passport valid at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand; a ticket out of New Zealand or proof you can afford one (unless the visa says return or onward travel is not required); funds of at least NZD 1,000 a month (NZD 400 a month if accommodation is prepaid); good health and character (a chest X-ray or medical exam may be requested, and police certificates may be needed for longer stays). INZ says 80% of applications are processed within 2 weeks; check current processing times before booking non-refundable travel. Everyone, including visa holders, must also complete the New Zealand Traveller Declaration before arrival.
fee_notes: INZ visitor visa page: from NZD 441. The October 2024 INZ fee table lists the visitor visa at NZD 300 (rest of world) plus a NZD 41 immigration levy (NZD 341), and the International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) is a separate non-refundable NZD 100, which gives NZD 441. The IVL is not refunded even if the application is declined.

conditions_text: New Zealand Electronic Travel Authority (NZeTA). Pre-travel online authorisation, in force today: Immigration New Zealand lists this passport (listed as United States of America, including USA nationals) as a visa waiver passport, so a visitor visa is not needed, but an NZeTA must be requested and granted before you travel (via the INZ website or the NZeTA mobile app; INZ says a request is issued within 72 hours). The NZeTA is valid for 2 years and covers multiple trips; you can stay up to 3 months per visit (entered here as 90 days), and no more than 6 months in any 12-month period. Conditions stated by INZ: passport valid at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand, and the same passport used for the NZeTA and for travel; a paid ticket out of New Zealand departing within the permitted stay; funds of at least NZD 1,000 a month (NZD 400 a month if accommodation is prepaid). Catches: you may not meet character requirements if you have a criminal conviction or have been deported, removed or excluded from another country, in which case a visitor visa application is the route; everyone must also complete the New Zealand Traveller Declaration (from 24 hours before travel by air).
fee_notes: NZeTA fee NZD 23 on the INZ website or NZD 17 in the mobile app (INZ), plus the non-refundable International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD 100 per person, paid with the request (NZD 100 since 1 October 2024; INZ does not refund the IVL even if the request is declined). Totals therefore NZD 123 (website) or NZD 117 (app) on the 2024 fee table rates.

conditions_text: Australian citizens do not need a visa or an NZeTA before travelling to New Zealand. INZ states you travel on a valid Australian passport (or an endorsed foreign passport), meet New Zealand's character requirements, and complete the New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD); on arrival you are normally granted an Australian Resident Visa, which lets you live, work and study in New Zealand, so no maximum stay applies. Catch: this is for Australian citizens. An Australian permanent resident who is not a citizen normally does need an NZeTA before travel (unless they already hold a valid New Zealand visa), plus a current Australian Permanent Resident Visa or Australian Resident Return Visa with travel conditions that allow return to Australia. Character requirements apply to both groups. The Australian Resident Visa ends each time you leave New Zealand, so residents planning a long absence should check INZ about a variation of travel conditions.
fee_notes: No visa or NZeTA fee for Australian citizens. INZ's IVL page lists holders of an Australian passport and Australian Resident Visa holders as exempt from the NZD 100 International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy. A non-citizen Australian permanent resident requesting an NZeTA: the INZ pages read did not state the fee or levy for that group; check the INZ fees tool.

Conditions stated by INZ: passport valid at least 3 months after the date you plan to leave New Zealand, and the same passport used for the NZeTA and for travel; a paid ticket out of New Zealand departing within the permitted stay; funds of at least NZD 1,000 a month (NZD 400 a month if accommodation is prepaid). Catches: you may not meet character requirements if you have a criminal conviction or have been deported, removed or excluded from another country, in which case a visitor visa application is the route; everyone must also complete the New Zealand Traveller Declaration (from 24 hours before travel by air).
fee_notes: NZeTA fee NZD 23 on the INZ website or NZD 17 in the mobile app (INZ), plus the non-refundable International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy (IVL) of NZD 100 per person, paid with the request (NZD 100 since 1 October 2024; INZ does not refund the IVL even if the request is declined). Totals therefore NZD 123 (website) or NZD 117 (app) on the 2024 fee table rates.

conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders need a visa before travelling to Brazil: the Foreign Ministry's Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos (updated 15 January 2026) marks India as visa required for a visit visa (VIVIS). The online e-Visa for tourism is only for US, Canadian and Australian passports; India's only e-visa is a business e-visa (stay of no more than 90 days, strictly business). A tourist visa must be applied for in person at the Brazilian Embassy in New Delhi, or at the Consulate General in Mumbai for residents of Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka, by appointment through the e-Consular system; courier applications are not accepted. The stay length for a tourist visa was not stated on the pages checked, so max stay is left empty. Visa fees are not refundable; no tourist-visa fee figure was found.

USA citizens need a visa to visit Brazil. Visa-free entry ended on 10 April 2025, and the online e-Visa (visitor visa, for tourism, business, transit and sporting or artistic activities) has been in force since that date; there is no future start date still pending. Apply online through the VFS portal (brazil.vfsevisa.com) before travelling; the Foreign Ministry's New York consulate page gives up to 90 days of stay, and it does not state whether that is per visit or per year (secondary sources say 90 days per visit within a 180-day yearly cap, which the official pages did not confirm). The e-Visa is only for visits, not residence or work; longer stays need a temporary visa from an embassy or consulate. Processing time is stated as about 5 working days by the Ciudad del Este consulate (other Brazilian missions give 10 or up to 15), so apply well ahead.
fee_notes: US$80.90 (stated on the Foreign Ministry's Ciudad del Este consulate page).

conditions_text: UK ordinary-passport holders can visit Brazil without a visa for up to 90 days (Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos, updated 15 January 2026: visa exemption for up to 90 days). Stays are for visiting purposes such as tourism and business meetings, not work.

German ordinary-passport holders can visit Brazil without a visa; the Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos (updated 15 January 2026) allows a maximum of 90 days of stay in any 180 days. Stays are for visiting purposes, not work.

Singapore ordinary-passport holders can visit Brazil without a visa for up to 30 days only (Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos, updated 15 January 2026), shorter than the 90 days given to UK and German passports. Longer stays need a visit visa applied for in advance.

Indian ordinary-passport holders may enter Argentina as tourists without a consular visa and without the electronic travel authorisation (AVE) if they hold a valid US visa in one of the listed categories (B1/B2, B2, J, B1, O, P1/P2/P3, E or H-1B) or a valid US permanent resident card (Green Card, accepted from 15 January 2026). This is Resolution 353/2025 of the Vice-Chief of Cabinet for the Interior, in force since 28 August 2025. The stay is up to 90 days, may be extended once by a similar period by Migraciones, and the category cannot be changed. The catch: the exemption does not apply to any other US visa type, it is for tourism only (other purposes need a consular visa), and Argentina's Embassy in India says the US visa or Green Card 'might' need at least 90 days of validity counted from the day you enter. Only a US document is documented as qualifying; the Embassy's page lists no concession for UK, Schengen, Canadian, Australian or Japanese visas. Passport: Argentina's consular pages state 6 months' validity and blank pages for visa applicants; no separate figure is stated for the visa-free route, so carry the same.
fee_notes: No fee: neither a visa nor an AVE is needed on this route.

conditions_text: Indian ordinary-passport holders without a qualifying US visa or Green Card (see the US-document row) must obtain an Argentine consular tourist visa before travel; Resolution 353/2025 Article 3 says everyone outside the US-visa exemption must apply for the corresponding consular visa. Apply at an Argentine embassy or consulate (the Embassy in New Delhi, the consulate in Mumbai, or any Argentine consulate worldwide). Maximum stay is 90 days. Argentine consular pages ask for a passport valid at least 6 months from the intended entry date with blank pages, a completed visa form, a photo, flight reservations in and out, hotel booking or an invitation, proof of funds (such as three months of bank statements) and an interview. Approval is at Argentina's discretion. No AVE route is described for Indian passports on the Embassy's page; AVE is for other nationalities who hold a US visa.
fee_notes: The Embassy states tourist visas are free for Indian nationals under a bilateral agreement (the standard fee for other nationalities is USD 150).

conditions_text: US citizens do not need a visa to visit Argentina for tourism or transit for up to 90 days. The stay can normally be extended once by a similar period at Migraciones (Argentina's immigration service). The reciprocity fee for US citizens has been suspended since 24 March 2016. Carry a valid passport for the whole stay; no onward-ticket rule for visa-free entry is stated on the cited page, so airlines may still ask for one.
fee_notes: No fee; the reciprocity fee has been suspended since 24 March 2016.

conditions_text: UK passport holders are on the Argentine Foreign Ministry's list of nationalities that need no visa to enter as tourists, for up to 90 days (extendable by a further 90 days). The cited list is an undated page published by the Argentine Embassy in Poland, so confirm against Migraciones' current nationality list before booking. No reciprocity fee is listed for UK citizens. Carry a passport valid for the stay.

Canadian citizens do not need a tourist visa to enter Argentina, and the Argentine Consulate in Montreal states they do not need to pay a reciprocity fee. The permitted tourist stay for visa-exempt nationals is 90 days. An older Argentine embassy list (undated) still carries a footnote about a Canadian reciprocity fee; the Montreal consulate page is the current statement. Carry a passport valid for the stay.
fee_notes: No reciprocity fee, per the Argentine Consulate in Montreal.

conditions_text: Australian citizens do not need a visa for tourist stays in Argentina of up to 90 days (Argentine Consulate General in Sydney). Medical insurance is recommended. Carry a passport valid for the stay.

German citizens do not need a visa to enter Argentina as tourists for up to 90 days (Argentine Embassy in Germany, tourist-visa page updated 11 July 2026). Argentina is not in the EU, so EU freedom of movement does not apply; this is Argentina's own visa exemption, and an extension of the stay is possible once at Migraciones. The page states a 6-month passport validity only for visa applicants and gives no separate rule for visa-free entry, so carry a passport valid for the stay.

Singaporean citizens do not require a visa to enter Argentina for tourism, for up to 90 days (Argentine Embassy in Singapore, AVE/entry page updated 27 November 2025). Carry a passport valid for the stay.

Brazilian citizens do not need a visa to enter Argentina as tourists, for up to 90 days (extendable by a further 90 days), per the Argentine Foreign Ministry's list of visa-exempt nationalities (an undated embassy-published list, so confirm on Migraciones' current page). Argentina's Migraciones tourist page also names a valid identity card among the accepted entry documents for Mercosur and associated-state nationals (citing Mercosur decision CMC 37/14); carry your passport as well, as airlines may insist on it.

Indian ordinary-passport holders are exempt from Chile's transitory-stay (tourist) visa if they hold a US visa of any type except type C (transit), valid for at least six months at the time of arrival in Chile, or a US Green Card (this row covers that US-document case; in force since 1 April 2019). The maximum stay is 90 days. The Chilean consulate in New Delhi says travellers must also show sufficient funds. Only a US document unlocks this: the consular table does not list a Canadian, UK, Australian or Schengen visa as a concession for Indian passports, so those holders still need the visa in the other India row. Check the US visa's remaining validity before booking.

Indian passport holders without a qualifying US visa (any type except C, valid at least six months on arrival) or US Green Card need a Chilean transitory-stay (tourist) visa issued by a Chilean consulate before travel. Chile's consular table lists a single-entry visa valid for up to 90 days and a multiple-entry visa with a maximum stay of 90 days. The New Delhi consulate page says processing takes several weeks and can take up to six months, and that applicants must apply to the consulate covering their residence (Mumbai for residents of other Indian states). Schengen, UK, Canadian or Australian visas do not exempt Indian passports (the only exemption in Chile's table is for US visas and Green Cards).
fee_notes: Consular fee per Chile's table: US$42 single entry, US$76 multiple entry.

Immigration (PDI) grants the permit on arrival (Tarjeta Unica Migratoria); the permit cannot run past your passport's expiry and you may be asked to show means to support your stay. Chile's own table lists no entry fee for this nationality.

Indian citizens are on Ecuador's Foreign Ministry list of nationalities that must have a visa to enter Ecuador (the list names India once; it is undated, and Ecuador's Madrid consulate page of 2 September 2025 repeats the same 45-country list for the transit visa). A tourist visa has to be applied for at an Ecuadorian consular office before travel; it is valid for 90 days from entry and can be extended once by up to 90 days (Regulation art. 97). The Washington consulate page and Regulation art. 97 list the requirements: passport valid at least 6 months, a criminal record certificate (apostilled or legalised), proof of lawful means of support, and a travel itinerary with return ticket. No concession was found: neither the Foreign Ministry list nor the consulate pages say that holding a US, UK, Schengen or other visa lets an Indian passport holder enter without an Ecuadorian visa, so none is encoded. Indian citizens also need a transit visa (applied for from abroad at least 20 days ahead) from 1 September 2025 for travel through Ecuadorian territory; the page does not say whether airport-only transit is covered, so confirm with a consulate before booking a connection.
fee_notes: Washington consulate page (undated) lists a USD 50 application fee plus USD 30 if approved; the Houston consulate page says the fee follows the Consular and Diplomatic Tariff. Confirm the current fee with the consulate.

conditions_text: Ecuador's Foreign Ministry list of nationalities that need a visa to enter does not include this passport, so a tourist is given a stay permit at the border migration control point with no visa. Tourists may stay up to 90 days in the one-year period counted from first entry, extendable once by up to 90 further days on application and payment of a fee (Regulation to the Organic Law on Human Mobility, art. 96; Law art. 56). Tourists may not work. Passport should be valid at least 6 months (ecuador.travel, the official tourism site). Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket. If you will visit the Galapagos you also need private health insurance, a Transit Control Card (USD 20, bought at the Quito or Guayaquil airport) and a Galapagos park entry fee.
fee_notes: No fee for the border stay permit. Extension beyond 90 days costs one third of the basic monthly wage (Interior Ministry page, USD 131.33 in 2019 terms).

conditions_text: UK citizens can visit Ecuador without a visa for up to 90 days in any 12-month period (UK FCDO entry requirements). An extra 90 days can be paid for inside Ecuador but the extension must be applied for before the first period ends. Passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival. At border control you may be asked for proof of a return or onward journey. For the Galapagos you need evidence of a return flight to the mainland, mandatory health insurance and the Transit Control Card bought at the departure airport before check-in.
fee_notes: No fee for the border stay permit; the 90-day extension is paid.

conditions_text: Canadian citizens do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 90 days per period of 12 months and can extend once for an additional 90 days (Global Affairs Canada). The passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the date you expect to leave Ecuador. For the Galapagos you must present a return ticket and buy the Transit Control Card at the Galapagos Governing Council counter in the Quito or Guayaquil airport.
fee_notes: No fee for the border stay permit; the 90-day extension is paid.

conditions_text: Brazil is not on Ecuador's Foreign Ministry visa-required list. Tourists may not work. Border officers may ask for a return or onward ticket. For the Galapagos you need private health insurance, a Transit Control Card (USD 20, bought at the Quito or Guayaquil airport) and the park entry fee (Brazilian nationals pay the reduced Mercosur rate of USD 100 for over-12s).
fee_notes: No fee for the border stay permit.

conditions_text: MIREX (Dominican Ministry of Foreign Affairs) visa-requirements lookup, ordinary passport, tourist visa, answers 'Requires visa? NO' for the United States. Tourism needs a valid passport and the tourist card. The stay allowed is up to 30 days (Dominican tax authority DGII's tourist-card page, dgii.gov.do/sobreTarjetaTurista/Paginas/preguntasFrecuentes.aspx); a longer stay needs a paid extension from the Dirección General de Migración (the Dominican tourism board, godominicanrepublic.com, says a fee is charged on departure for stays beyond 30 days). Foreign visitors on commercial flights must also complete the free electronic entry/exit form (E-ticket) at eticket.migracion.gob.do before check-in, and the tourism board states airlines must see a round-trip air ticket for every foreign passenger (rule since 28 April 2023), a Dominican address and proof of funds may be asked for. Tourism only: the tourist card does not cover work or study. Passport: the tourism board's entry-requirements page states six months' validity as the general rule, but a temporary measure (1 December 2024 to 31 December 2026, so in force today and due to end) lets nationals of the EU, UK, Canada, USA, Brazil, Chile, Argentina, Colombia and Ecuador enter for tourism with a passport that is valid for the stay and departure. Airlines may apply their own stricter rule; after 31 December 2026 check again.
fee_notes: Tourist card US$10 (or EUR 10 at sea and land borders), a tax set by Law 199-67; for air arrivals it is included in the airfare, so you do not pay it separately (DGII page above). The tourism board also states the US$20 departure tax is already included in the airline ticket. Fees can change; confirm with your airline.

conditions_text: Visa on arrival, no advance application needed. Visa on arrival at Queen Alia International Airport (Amman) and the Sheikh Hussein Bridge crossing; Wadi Araba (Eilat-Aqaba) only for Jordan Pass holders who stay the minimum nights; the King Hussein (Allenby) Bridge requires a visa obtained beforehand (Global Affairs Canada). Jordan's Ministry of Interior restricted-nationalities list (updated 9 November 2025) does not include India, so no prior approval is listed for this passport. Passport validity: the UK and Canadian governments both advise at least 6 months, so carry at least that. Jordan Pass visa waiver: the official Jordan Pass site says you must stay at least 2 whole nights (3 days); the UK government and Visit Jordan describe it as 3 nights, so plan 3 nights to be safe. Immigration checks your nights on exit and sends you to an office to pay the fee if you fell short. Aqaba rule (ASEZA): arriving by the Aqaba port, airport or a land border (except the southern Wadi Araba crossing) gives a free visa if you leave within one month through the same border. Entering elsewhere and heading to Aqaba, you can claim it by declaring Aqaba as your destination and registering at the ASEZA visa office in Aqaba within 48 hours, otherwise you pay for the visa plus a fine of 1.5 JOD per unregistered day (visitaqaba.com, undated page, which says rules may change). Length of stay: the Jordan Pass FAQ says the single-entry visa is valid for 1 month and extendable; the UK government and Global Affairs Canada say 3 months, so no day count is encoded here; confirm at the border. India: the Indian Embassy in Amman links a Jordanian Ministry of Interior e-visa portal (eservices.moi.gov.jo) in a guidance document, but its terms could not be opened and are not relied on; no Jordanian page read says India needs an advance visa, and India is not on the restricted list.
fee_notes: Single-entry tourist visa on arrival is 40 JOD (about 60 USD per the Jordan Pass FAQ; the UK government also gives 40 JOD). The Jordan Pass (Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities; Wanderer 70 JOD, Explorer 75 JOD, Expert 80 JOD, with 1, 2 or 3 consecutive days at Petra) includes the visa fee. The waiver covers only a single-entry visa and requires buying the pass before arrival. Visa extension: 3 JOD per extra day paid at the airport, or 40 JOD at a police station for 2 months (Jordan Pass FAQ).

conditions_text: Kenya replaced visas with the Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) in January 2024, and it is in force today: apply online before you travel, only through the official portal etakenya.go.ke (the Kenyan embassy in Vienna warns that look-alike sites are automatically denied). Kenya's embassy says the eTA is mandatory for all foreign visitors except listed groups (citizens of East African Community states, Kenyan citizens and residents, transit passengers who stay airside, some official passport holders and others); this passport is not exempt, and being a Commonwealth citizen does not exempt you. Official guidance: apply at least 3 days before travel (embassy; standard processing 3 working days) and FCDO recommends at least 2 weeks. An approved eTA must be used to enter within 90 days of issue and is generally single-entry (short trips to Burundi, DR Congo, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania or Uganda do not need a new one). The visitor's pass can be extended at a Kenyan immigration office by up to 90 days, then a further 90 days, with a total stay capped at 180 days; the length of the initial stay granted is not stated on the pages checked, so max_stay_days is left empty. Indian passport holders are not on any exemption list. Passport: UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada both say at least 6 months' validity from arrival (FCDO also says 2 blank pages); the Kenyan embassy page lists only 'a valid passport', so follow the stricter rule. New: from 5 October 2026 most visitors staying under 12 months must buy Kenyan Government travel health insurance during the eTA application (foreign policies are not accepted; valid 90 days; EAC citizens exempt) per FCDO and Global Affairs Canada. Yellow fever vaccination proof is required if arriving from a country where it occurs (Global Affairs Canada).
fee_notes: Fee amount is not stated on any official page that could be opened (etakenya.go.ke renders client-side and returned no text; embassy pages omit the amount): the portal shows it before payment. Card payment only. Fee waived for official/diplomatic passports on duty and nationals of Comoros, Congo-Brazzaville, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Mozambique, San Marino and South Africa (not this passport). Mandatory government travel health insurance is bought in addition (price not stated on pages checked).

conditions_text: India is on Tanzania's list of nationalities eligible for both online and on-arrival visas, and the guidelines explicitly exclude India from the Commonwealth visa exemption. Ordinary (single-entry) tourist visa, valid for up to 90 days. Two routes, both official: apply online at visa.immigration.go.tz (the portal says this is the recommended route; processing is stated as within ten days, and you carry the Visa Grant Notice), or get the same visa on arrival at an official entry point. UK FCDO notes visa on arrival is single entry only at main ports of entry. Passport: Tanzania Immigration's guidelines require at least six months' validity and at least one unused visa page, and say visitors must show a return ticket on arrival. Visa grant notice is not a final right of entry; the immigration officer at the border can still refuse. Zanzibar: one visa covers both the mainland and Zanzibar, and the portal says to select your first destination on the form. Mandatory inbound travel insurance (separate from the visa; not on the immigration portal): a Zanzibar Insurance Corporation public notice dated 7 October 2026 says it applies to foreign visitors entering the mainland from 1 October 2026, is bought for your first point of entry (ZIC at inbound.visitzanzibar.go.tz if you land in Zanzibar first; National Insurance Corporation at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz if you land on the mainland), covers 92 days with no second policy needed for mainland plus Zanzibar within that period, and you must keep the certificate and QR code for scanning. Qualifying EAC and SADC travellers are exempt on the mainland. The premium was not verified. Yellow fever: a certificate is required if you arrive from, or spent over 12 hours in transit in, a country with yellow fever transmission risk (CDC; FCDO). Rules can change without notice.
fee_notes: Ordinary visa USD 50 (immigration.go.tz service-fee table and eVisa guidelines); paid online by Visa or Mastercard card. On-arrival payment method was not stated on the pages checked.
